existing_issues.issue: Title wording is wrong: Op. 1 has no 'Book 1'. It is one school in four parts (Bosworth 'Part', Schirmer 'Book', Bärenreiter 'Vol.'): 1 first position, 2 positions 2–7, 3 shifting, 4 double/triple/quadruple stops, left-hand pizzicato and harmonics. 'Book 1 Part 4' misreads as Book 1 of something. Also the set is empty, so the four parts cannot be grouped (use set 'School of Violin Technique, Op. 1'), and the notes omit chords and harmonics (suggest 'Double stops, chords, left-hand pizzicato and harmonics'). Level 7 is fine.
existing_issues.suggested_title: School of Violin Technique, Op. 1 Part 4 (double stops)

new_authors_found: Hidden, Reginald L. — 'Special Scales and Exercises for Violin' (Prague, Edition M.U. No. 276, 1906), dedicated to Ševčík; scale book on IMSLP (for the scales researchers)
note: WHAT THE SOURCES SAY. IMSLP's author category holds only 16 pages; the fuller list is IMSLP 'List of works by Otakar Ševčík' (Op. 1–26), which I cross-checked against the Czech National Library catalogue (NKČR, 361 records for the author; direct-record URLs in `source`), Bärenreiter UK, Hal Leonard/Bosworth (Music Sales) pages and the Internet Archive scans of the Harms Op. 11 and Bosworth Op. 1 editions. Czech Wikipedia's opus list (from Macková's thesis) matches the titles but gives no publication status. PARTS. Op. 1 = 4 parts; Op. 2 = 6 Hefte (Bosworth, Music Sales, IMSLP; Bärenreiter regroups them into 3 volumes: Parts 1–2, 3–4, 5–6); Op. 7 = 2 parts (Bärenreiter: one volume); Op. 11 = 17 booklets per Internet Archive cataloguing (Parts I, IIa, IIb, III, IV, V, VIa–c, VII–XIV, priced by the part; an NKČR variant record says 'XV parts and two supplements'), of which V–XIV are reported; Op. 16 = 2 parts (30 + 15 numbered booklets); Op. 26 = 4 volumes (Edition Pazdírek 557–560). Bosworth's 1956 'Op. 1a' abridged edition by Maxim Jacobsen (Internet Archive scan) is NOT the original: its Part 1 spans 1st–3rd positions, whereas the original Part 1 (Bosworth/Sachania, Schirmer, Bärenreiter, IMSLP) is first position only. NOT PUBLISHED / UNVERIFIED. Op. 12–15 (never published), Op. 22–24 and the Dvořák studies are manuscripts; Op. 4 (1999 Arco Iris, per IMSLP only) and Op. 5 (revised by Kocian) have no catalogue record. LEVELS. No ABRSM/RCM/ASTA placement for any Ševčík part was found. Evidence used: Eastman Community Violin Curriculum (Op. 1 Pt 1 at Levels II–III; the school at Levels IV–VI), Bärenreiter difficulty labels (Op. 2 easy/moderate/difficult; Op. 7 moderate to advanced; Op. 8 moderate; Op. 3 medium to high), Ševčík's own grading in Op. 11 (Books II/III/IV elementary/intermediate/advanced; Parts XIII–XIV paired with Grade III–IV pieces), and the catalogue anchors (Op. 8 = 5, Op. 9 = 4, Op. 1 Part 4 = 7). Op. 11 and Op. 26 levels are inferred from contents; Op. 6 Parts 6–7 are borderline to the floor. ENTRIES WITH LIMITS. Op. 2 Part 4 and Part 6 content details come from Music Sales' cello-edition blurbs (same six-part layout); I did not see the violin Hefte. Op. 25, Op. 26 and 'Scales and Arpeggios' (Tonleitern und Akkord-Studien, Bosworth c1911) are each backed by one library or publisher record (medium confidence); I could not see their contents, and for Op. 26 the étude range per volume is unknown. NOT READ. The theses by Hejnová (Masaryk Univ.), Macková (Charles Univ.) and Burczyk sit behind a cookie/JavaScript gate or returned 404, and I did not work around it; HathiTrust is behind a Cloudflare challenge. Google Books API was rate-limited. Web searches used: 4 of the 6–8 allowed. Existing ids 2114 (Op. 8) and 2115 (Op. 9) are correct as they stand.
